items.title: Barney Bigard Interview, 1969-07-25
items.q: And it's going to be the same thing with Louis Armstrong.

ctx.x: Hi Bill, this is Floyd Levin in Los Angeles. This is the 25th of July 1969 and shortly I expect Barney Begard over, at which time I will supply the questions and hopefully he'll come up with some of the answers to help you on your quest for information about Jelly Roll Morton. Okay, we've just played the Victor Trio session, Barney. I assume that you have some memories about that session. Yeah, I was really surprised. I thought I played more than I do now. That's going back, what, 40 years? Yes, it is. Could you…

items.title: 52986_Lawrence Brown oral history interview
items.q: thing, when I left Louis Armstrong and I went to get my unemployment

ctx.x: -- all of these things are just too bad.

-- thing, when I left Louis Armstrong and I went to get my unemployment and I put it in and because New York and California, at that time, you worked together, you know for unemployment, so when the -- you have to wait two weeks before you get it and so after two weeks I went over -- nothing for me, so I say, well maybe they didn't straighten out the -- the guys says fill out your thing for next week. So I fill it out -- fill them out for about 12 weeks and then, I'm not getting anything. So one day, what

is this business? So the guy says -- says let's go in the back he wanted to talk he left his cage and give it to somebody else. So we sat down and we talked and he says, well, New York says they haven't got anything on -- on you. So I said well that's funny, so I says, what do you mean they don't have anything? And I was telling him my case, you know, so that I didn't know that Frenchy was stealing all -- just little insignificant money every week, you know. items.title: Barney Bigard Interview, Early 1970s
items.q: I made them all with Duke, I made some of my own, I made some with Freddie Slight, and I made a lot of them with Louie.

ctx.x: Do you have any idea how many records you may have recorded over the years? Oh, not the faintest idea.

You lost count after 5,000 I bet. Oh, easy. I made them all with Duke, I made some of my own, I made some with Freddie Slight, and I made a lot of them with Louie. And I made a lot of different groups, you know, like on the side, what do you call a sideline, you know, one of those deals. And made a lot of studio recordings.

So it's pretty high. You know, we've had a number of people on the show, and we've talked to them about jazz, or swing, or big bands, or whatever you want to call it. And it would seem to me that you would be the man that would know the origin of such terms as jazz. Because you were born originally down there in the Crescent City itself, weren't you?
